item.title: Elliptic soliton solutions of lattice eigenfunction equations of the KdV type
item.description: arXiv:2610.41088v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: It is known that some integrable lattice equations can be formulated by the eigenfunctions of the Lax triplet of the lattice potential Korteweg-de Vries (lpKdV) equation; the eigenfunctions satisfy a discrete Abel formula in which the `integration' constant defines the $\delta$ parameter in some equations in the Adler-Bobenko-Suris (ABS) classification. In this paper, we present a full Darboux transformation for the Lax triplet of the lpKdV equation, and eigenfunctions are formulated in terms of Casoratians. When the eigenfunctions take the elementary discrete Lam\'e functions, we get the elliptic $N$-soliton solution for the lpKdV equation after $N$-fold Darboux transformation. We then determine the constant in the discrete Abel formula in this case. The eigenfunctions are used to formulate elliptic $N$-soliton solutions for various equations in the ABS list, such as H3($\delta$), $Q1(\Delta)$, Q2 and Q3($\Delta$) equations.
item.dc:creator: Xing Li, Ying Shi, Da-jun Zhang, Ruixiao Zhu

item.title: Root-of-unity limit of the $A_{n-1}$ lens elliptic gamma function solution of the star-star relation
item.description: arXiv:2610.41438v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the root-of-unity limit of the multi-component spin solution of the star-star relation whose Boltzmann weights are products of lens elliptic gamma functions, and whose spins take values in $\mathbb{R}^{n-1}\times(\mathbb{Z}_r)^{n-1}$. When one of the elliptic nomes tends to a primitive $2rN$-th root of unity, the quasi-classical expansion gives at leading order the classical star-star relation of the Bazhanov-Sergeev multi-spin model; at the next order, under the standard assumptions on the saddle points, a $(\mathbb{Z}_{rN})^{n-1}$-state solution of the star-star relation, which depends on $r$ and $N$ only through $rN$. Real $\mathbb{Z}_n$-symmetric configurations of the continuous spins give elliptic $\mathfrak{sl}(n)$ Kashiwara-Miwa type models labeled by $n$-torsion points. Extended to general primitive torsion points, these include the broken $\mathbb{Z}_{rN}$ model of Quano and Fujii, for which the star-star relation follows from their Yang-Baxter equation when $\gcd(n,rN)=1$. In the trigonometric limit the saddle point equations single out the spectral curve of the $\mathfrak{sl}(n)$ chiral Potts model of Bazhanov, Kashaev, Mangazeev and Stroganov, and the Boltzmann weights become those of that model.
item.dc:creator: Masahito Yamazaki

item.title: Open WDVV equations and $\bigvee$-systems
item.description: arXiv:2604.14077v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The idea of a $\bigvee$-system was introduced by Veselov in the study of rational solutions of the WDVV equations of associativity. These are algebraic/geometric conditions on the set of covectors that appear in rational solutions to the WDVV equations. Here, this idea is generalized to open WDVV equations, which are an additional set of PDEs originating from open Gromow-Witten Theory. We develop -- for rank-one extensions -- algebraic/geometric conditions on the covectors that supplement the $\bigvee$-system to give rational solutions to the open WDVV equations. Examples, and the relation to superpotentials and to Dubrovin almost-duality, are given.
item.dc:creator: Alessandro Proserpio, Ian A. B. Strachan
